Topic 8.2: Bracelet making ORNAMENTS

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Bracelet making ORNAMENTS. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How did you make your enjoyment making bracelet?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate own and others collection and in making finished work. bracelets. • display the made bracelets, appreciate own and others work

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BRACELET MAKING ORNAMENTS
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Bracelet making ORNAMENTS helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BRACELET MAKING ORNAMENTS
Study Bracelet making ORNAMENTS like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Appreciate own and others collection and in making finished work. bracelets. • display the made bracelets, appreciate own and others work

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate own and others collection and in making finished work. bracelets. • display the made bracelets, appreciate own and others work. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate own and others collection and in making finished work. bracelets. • display the made bracelets, appreciate own and others work.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Bracelet making ORNAMENTS” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate own and others collection and in making finished work. bracelets. • display the made bracelets, appreciate own and others work. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Bracelet making ORNAMENTS is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Bracelet making ORNAMENTS” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate own and others collection and in making finished work. bracelets. • display the made bracelets, appreciate own and others work)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Bracelet making ORNAMENTS to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate own and others collection and in making finished work. bracelets. • display the made bracelets, appreciate own and others work.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Bracelet making ORNAMENTS from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Bracelet making ORNAMENTS: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Bracelet making ORNAMENTS?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How did you make your enjoyment making bracelet?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Bracelet making ORNAMENTS means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate own and others collection and in making finished work. bracelets. • display the made bracelets, appreciate own and others work.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
